active_family: 631 incumbent native joint increment base; 638 level-score branch retained as coordinate milestone
current_bottleneck: There is a clean coordinate tradeoff. 631a/629a encoded-increment generation preserves anchor-factor and IV-factor joint behavior but accumulates IV level drift/explosions. 638a level-score generation fixes IV support/tails/cross-cell structure but damages anchor-factor changes and joint co-movement. The bottleneck is whether a fixed, training-data-justified generated-coordinate policy can handle heterogeneous financial variables while remaining one shared model.
last_result_summary: 639a ideated the only acceptable mixed-coordinate path. A mixed generated coordinate is principled only if framed as data-coordinate selection, not as separate IV/factor models: one shared memory, one velocity network, one checkpoint, one stochastic rollout, but each channel's generated stochastic variable is selected by a fixed variable spec. Hard-coding IV vs factor is scientifically weaker; the cleaner next move is a coordinate-policy audit using training-only stationarity/support diagnostics and 631a/638a failure signatures.
next_step_recommendation: Run 640a as a coordinate-policy audit before implementing a mixed-coordinate model. Compute per-channel diagnostics comparing level-score deltas versus encoded increments, then decide whether a fixed generated-coordinate map is simple and defensible enough for a later 641a mixed-coordinate transition.
